item3_pin_failure_modes.missing: reuse + loud note (PIN DEGRADED (absent) ... UNVERIFIED): a fresh setup has no pin yet; refusing would hard-fail every pre-pin/scratch setup, and absence cannot be distinguished from deletion without breaking the documented control boundary
item3_pin_failure_modes.malformed: refuse (pin malformed): the file exists and cannot be honoured; a present-and-broken control must not equal 'no pin'
item3_pin_failure_modes.unreadable: refuse (pin unreadable, e.g. chmod 000 / EISDIR): same argument - interference or corruption, not absence
item3_pin_failure_modes.other_path: reuse + loud note (PIN DEGRADED (no_entry)): a well-formed committed pin may legitimately cover other targets; no expectation exists for THIS artifact, and the loud note is the mitigation
item3_pin_failure_modes.empty: refuse (pin empty): an entry for this exact path with no usable value is a recorded expectation that cannot be checked (and an easy way to launder a deletion)
item3_pin_failure_modes.now_loud: note added: 'graph: PIN DEGRADED (<state>): ... UNVERIFIED and reused anyway; this is a degraded control, not a verified match' for the reuse cases; refusals go to ctx.graph_rejected AND notes ('pin <state>: ... the graph is NOT reused'). The stage line also carries '(no pin recorded [<state>] ...)'
item3_pin_failure_modes.justification: The flag means 'do not trust a graph I cannot vouch for'; an unverified graph (no recorded built_at_commit, or an unreadable target HEAD) is exactly that, so the opt-in now refuses it too - it is opt-in, so the default report-only reuse is untouched and the genuine graph is STALE (not unverified), so the real path is unaffected.
